input.quote: If any difference shall arise between or among the Parties or any of them in respect of the interpretation or effect of this Agreement or any part or provision thereof or their rights and obligations thereunder, and by reasons thereof there shall arise the need to decide the question by what municipal or national law this Agreement or any part or provision thereof is governed, the following facts shall be excluded from consideration
input.rationale: The Agreement has no governing law or venue provision. §27.2 does the opposite of designating a law: it merely strips away connecting factors that a court might otherwise use to identify the applicable municipal or national law, leaving the governing law deliberately undetermined. §27.1 makes referral to the Management Committee — which may itself elect arbitration by an unspecified method and seat — the sole and exclusive remedy, so there is also no court forum. Nothing in the document reaches either the preferred (New York law and New York County courts) or the fallback (Delaware/California, or England and Wales with London courts) position, and the open-ended arbitration discretion risks a foreign seat. We propose inserting a new §27.3 fixing New York law and exclusive New York County court jurisdiction, leaving §27.1 and §27.2 otherwise intact.

proposal.summary: Add express New York governing law and exclusive New York County court venue.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no governing law or venue provision, and §27 leaves disputes to the Management Committee (which may impose arbitration) as the sole remedy. We have added our standard position: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County; Delaware, California or England and Wales with the courts of London would also work for us.

ops.text: 27.3 This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, and the Parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York in respect of any dispute arising under or in connection with this Agreement.
